subject: Climate & Environment
title: Fossil Fuel Subsidies
description: Learn Fossil Fuel Subsidies in one minute.

hook.text: Governments worldwide spend over $7 trillion a year supporting fossil fuels.

buildup.text: That includes direct payments, tax breaks, and not charging for pollution damage.

discovery.text: Removing subsidies would make renewables even more competitive overnight.

twist.text: But cheap fuel keeps millions out of energy poverty — cutting subsidies hurts the poor first.

climax.text: Smart reforms redirect subsidies to clean energy and protect vulnerable households.

punchline.text: We subsidize the problem and wonder why it won't go away.

quiz.question: How much do governments spend supporting fossil fuels annually?

details.summary: Governments worldwide spent over $7 trillion in 2022 on direct and indirect fossil fuel subsidies, including underpriced environmental and health damages. These subsidies distort energy markets, slow the renewable transition, and effectively pay polluters while clean energy competes on uneven terms.
details.whyItMatters: Fossil fuel subsidies are one of the biggest obstacles to the energy transition. Redirecting even a fraction could fund massive renewable deployment and climate adaptation.
takeaways: Global fossil fuel subsidies exceeded $7 trillion in 2022
Subsidies include tax breaks and unpriced pollution damages
Removing them would accelerate the renewable energy transition

faq.question: Why do governments subsidize fossil fuels?
faq.answer: Subsidies keep energy affordable for consumers and protect domestic industries. In many developing countries, fuel subsidies prevent energy poverty. Politically, removing subsidies is unpopular and risks public backlash, even when alternatives exist.

faq.question: How do fossil fuel subsidies slow the renewable transition?
faq.answer: By artificially cheapening fossil fuels, subsidies make renewables appear less competitive. They also lock in fossil infrastructure investment. The IMF estimates that eliminating subsidies would cut global CO2 emissions by over 30 percent.
